Trump signals de-escalation with Iran, oil prices fall

US President Donald Trump has indicated that renewed military strikes on Iran are "highly unlikely" if talks progress, suggesting the conflict is "effectively over." This de-escalation has led to a significant drop in oil prices, with crude oil holding near $90 per barrel and falling to a two-month low. Indian markets rallied on November 5, with the Sensex and Nifty surging nearly 2 percent, attributed to the easing of US-Iran war tensions and the US midterm election results where Democrats won control of both chambers of Congress. Iran's Mohsen Rezaei reportedly issued seven conditions for ending the war. Meanwhile, there are reports of Iran distributing iodine tablets near nuclear sites, and an open letter to Donald Trump urged him to prevent Iran from acquiring nuclear weapons.
